what: The photo is attached to a convex plate whose center bulges forward by .176 of the plate height, and drawn in perspective (eye distance 2.6). It tilts up to .42 rad on the X axis and .5 rad on the Y axis according to how far the plate is from screen center (one screen up or down maps to −1 to 1). Entering from below, it tilts back and leans at a slant. At center it faces straight on. Leaving upward, it leans the opposite way. The plate frame stays put and only the picture inside spins in space, with a faint glaze-like reflection (.2) catching the upper-left light. The picture is fitted at .84x inside the plate so the edges never show empty space.

options.tilt: Max tilt angle on the X axis (rad), default .42
options.turn: Max rotation angle around the Y axis (rad), default .5
options.dome: How much the center bulges (ratio to panel height), default .176 — 0 makes a flat panel
options.flip: 1 turns in reverse on the Y axis — for alternating left and right photos

note: Image child (data-fx-part="img") is missing, draws a data-label placeholder in skin colors (--kf-surface · --kf-line · --kf-dim) sized to the panel so the bend is visible. The shader is precompiled on attach and redraws only while on screen (20% margin before and after). Without WebGL nothing is hooked, so the panel’s gray surface and image stay as they are. With reduced motion, only one upright panel is drawn

from.where: index.html .case .pic — the original pastes four case photos onto a convex plate with a shader and spins it on scroll (CSS plate is rotateX 13°·rotateY ±9°·1.24×)
